title: The Generalized BEADS Representation: An Informationally Complete Visualization of Mixed Quantum States
authors: Celina Bräutigam, Steffen J. Glaser, Dennis Huber
abstract: A deep understanding of quantum information theory is essential for quantum science and technology. However, quantum mechanics and particularly quantum information theory suffer from a lack of intuitive images. Visualization tools offer novel perspectives on many problems in quantum physics by revealing important properties of quantum states and processes that are otherwise obscured by abstract mathematical formalisms. Here, we extend the previously established BEADS representation of pure states to the so-called generalized BEADS representation of mixed quantum states. We introduce spherical functions, so-called beads to visualize correlation structures of mixed quantum states. A recursive optimization scheme is used to obtain minimum-entanglement pure state decompositions of all subsystems of a given N-qubit state. We show how correlation function components can be decomposed into individual contributions that directly correspond to different types of correlations of mixed states. This allows us to visually characterize the total correlation, genuine n-partite entanglement, nonclassical quantum-discord-type correlations as well as classical correlations. After outlining the mathematical details relevant for constructing the representation, we examine the generalized BEADS representations for various classes of mixed states including product, classically correlated, separable but nonclassically correlated, as well as entangled states. As exemplary applications of the generalized BEADS representation, we showcase entanglement distillation and the effects of noise channels.
summary: This paper introduces the generalized BEADS representation, an advanced visualization technique, to overcome the abstract mathematical difficulties in analyzing mixed quantum states. It allows researchers to visually separate and quantify different types of quantum correlations, such as genuine entanglement and classical correlations. This tool proves superior to existing diagnostic methods like sector length analysis by directly mapping the underlying correlation structure.
main_problem: The primary challenge is the lack of intuitive visualization tools for understanding the complex correlation structures within mixed quantum states.
main_result: The generalized BEADS representation successfully provides a visual framework to decompose and characterize total correlation, genuine n-partite entanglement, and classical correlations in mixed states.
method: The authors extend the BEADS visualization tool by using spherical functions ('beads') and a recursive optimization scheme to decompose the density operator into contributions corresponding to different correlation types.
model_or_system: The study focuses on N-qubit mixed quantum states ($ho$), comparing the visualization power of the generalized BEADS representation against traditional methods like sector length analysis.
key_observables: Total correlation, genuine n-partite entanglement, classical correlations, quantum discord, and sector lengths ($A_k$).
important_parameters: The number of qubits (N), the mixing parameters ($p$), and the linearity parameter ($g$) used in the bead visualization.
main_assumptions: The method assumes that correlation structures can be decomposed into distinct, visually identifiable components (e.g., separable vs. entangled contributions).
figures_summary: Figures compare the generalized BEADS visualization (using color coding for separable/entangled structure) against the results from sector length analysis for various mixed states, demonstrating where BEADS provides superior diagnostic power.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the generalized BEADS representation for mixed states, details the mathematical decomposition of correlation functions, and then contrasts its diagnostic power against sector length analysis using multiple examples of three-qubit states.
why_interesting: It provides a powerful, intuitive visualization tool for complex quantum correlations in mixed states, which is crucial for understanding noise, entanglement distillation, and open quantum system dynamics.

Figure 3: Overview of the entirety of bead types for ρproduct (see Eq. (29)). In the generalized BEADS picture, it is directly clear that the state is not genuinely correlated as there are no M-Beads. The T- and C-Beads are identical, but only encode redundant information, that is the products of the single-qubit reduced density operators Q1 and Q2.

Figure 4: E-Beads representation of an optimized pure state decomposition of ρproduct. Indeed, the pure states do not show any E-Beads for which they are uncorrelated product states. As a direct consequence, the corresponding mixed state does also not show any E-Beads as these result as convex sums of the pure state E-Beads, which here are zero in all spatial directions. The weights and two-tangles of each pure state are plotted in the top left corner of every state’s subfigure.

Figure 5: Complete generalized BEADS representation of the classical-classical state ρclass-class (Eq. (31)). Although the state has no total correlation function (T-Beads), it is still genuinely correlated (M-Bead). Since there are no E-Beads, all genuine correlations arise from the separable structure of the state, which is reflected in identical M- and Σ-Beads. Coinciding M (1) Cl -, Σ(1) Cl -, Σ- and M-Beads allow to unambiguously identify the state as being classically correlated with respect to an optimized local measurement of qubit 1. Figure 6 provides the full generalized BEADS representation of the discussed state. Again, as the state is separable, all E-Beads vanish and T- and the C-Beads result in being identical. In this case the Q-Beads are all-black, which implies that the reduced single-qubit density operators are maximally mixed and do not encode any information. Thus, the entire information encoded on the correlation function beads corresponds to genuine correlations of the state and T-, C-, M-, and Σ-Beads all coincide consequently.
